title: Jalapeño Cheddar Smoked Sausages
seoTitle: Jalapeño Cheddar Smoked Sausages | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Smoked links with cheese and heat—fast line, big flavor
subtitle: Smoked links, pepper jack melt, and grilled peppers for ten
description: Adapted from classic smoked sausage platter tradition (Traeger, Weber): jalapeño-cheddar links smoke at 275°F until 165°F internal, then grill with peppers and onions for a handheld tray.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Jalapeño Cheddar Smoked Sausages in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use neutral oil as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Prep the links
steps.instruction: Score sausage casings lightly. Toss peppers and onions with oil, salt, and pepper. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Smoke at 275°F
steps.instruction: Smoke sausages at 275°F until internal temp reaches 155°F, about 30–35 minutes. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Grill finish
steps.instruction: Grill sausages and peppers over medium-high 8–10 minutes until links hit 165°F and peppers char lightly. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest links 3 minutes. Transfer to a covered pan with peppers and onions. Hold at 170°F until service. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Toast rolls
steps.instruction: Split rolls and toast cut-side down on the grill 1 minute until marked. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F with a 3-minute rest on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Cooking step
steps.instruction: Sausages and peppers in a pan, rolls, mustard, pickled jalapeños. Build-your-own sandwich line. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew.

steps.title: Leftovers
steps.instruction: Slice into a breakfast scramble with eggs. Reheat covered at 325°F until 165°F. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: 165°F internal on sausage—don't guess by color alone.
Score casings so they don't burst on the grill finish.
Pickled jalapeños add acid that balances rich cheese links.
tonightSpread: Smoked links with peppers and onions in a hotel pan.
Toasted rolls, mustard, and pickled jalapeños.
leftovers: Sausage and pepper hoagies with extra mustard.
Chop into a smoky pasta skillet with cream.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sausage night is zero drama. Links hold covered at 170°F, and the line moves fast with buns or tortillas.
mealPrepNotes: Score links lightly before smoking. Smoke ahead, then grill-mark before service. Hold in a covered pan at 170°F with peppers.
